findings.title: Zero-net scroll retains the previous burst clock
findings.reproduction: Scroll +1 at1000, -1 at1100, flush1500, then +1 at5000 and flush5400.
findings.root_cause: KL_Mouse_FlushScroll in static/ergopti_plus/windows/modules/keystats/keystats_mouse.ahk: The empty-delta return precedes clearing scroll_start and scroll_last.
findings.silent_failure: The next burst duration is4400 instead of400; the empty fixture starts with zero timestamps.
findings.regression_test: Assert timestamp retirement and the next burst duration through actual accumulate/flush ports.

findings.title: ROI word candidates miss special keys
findings.reproduction: Type hello, Enter, world and space; separately type hellox, Backspace and space.
findings.root_cause: _KL_Hook_CommitInput in static/ergopti_plus/windows/modules/keystats/keystats_hook.ahk: Only char intents reach ROI; Enter, Tab and Backspace are key intents.
findings.silent_failure: ROI records helloworld or hellox while typing-buffer tests cover only actual text.
findings.regression_test: Drive actual key/char owners and assert separate and corrected ROI candidates; exclude synthetic and private input.

findings.title: Zero-saving hotstring fires are absent from usage history
findings.reproduction: Fire an initialized public trigger with net_saved0 after an older positive-saving use.
findings.root_cause: KL_Roi_OnHotstring in static/ergopti_plus/windows/modules/keystats/keystats_trigger_roi.ahk: A nonpositive-savings guard suppresses independent fired-count and last-use bookkeeping.
findings.silent_failure: The active trigger retains an old last-use timestamp and can be reported stale.
findings.regression_test: Assert zero and negative savings fires update usage but add no positive savings; keep private trigger exclusion.

findings.title: Selected composition removal publishes duplicate results
findings.reproduction: Remove the selected composition; after invokes its refusal callback and returns false.
findings.root_cause: _LayoutComposer_Remove in static/ergopti_plus/windows/ui/layout_manager/composer.ahk: Unlike the save sibling, removal lacks a terminal Completed guard.
findings.silent_failure: Each callback and the fallback publish composerResult and updateState.
findings.regression_test: Inject duplicate refusal callbacks plus a false return and require exactly one result and one state push.

findings.title: Old layout operations publish into a replacement window
findings.reproduction: Start installation in session A; close A and open B; deliver the failure callback from A.
findings.root_cause: _LayMgrWeb_OnDone in static/ergopti_plus/windows/ui/layout_manager/init.ahk: Callbacks capture dependencies but no session epoch, and push targets the current global WebView.
findings.silent_failure: The old result overwrites the replacement session result and displays there.
findings.regression_test: Retain callback A, replace the session, complete A and assert no stale UI/result publication while durable work completes.

findings.title: Replacing the click watcher can strand an existing held button
findings.reproduction: Hold left click, request right hold by touch, and refuse construction or start of the replacement keyboard watcher.
findings.root_cause: GestureStartKeyboardWatcher in static/ergopti_plus/windows/modules/gestures/click.ahk: The active shared watcher is stopped before the replacement is acquired; rollback preserves the first held button.
findings.silent_failure: The next key has no observer to release the synthetic held button.
findings.regression_test: Retain an active watcher across overlapping holds; test both button orders and failed cleanup ownership.

findings.title: Output-only API usage has a zero total
findings.reproduction: Parse usage prompt_tokens0 completion_tokens10 without total_tokens; repeat Anthropic and Gemini equivalents.
findings.root_cause: _LLMRemoteExtractUsageRoot in static/ergopti_plus/windows/modules/llm/api_remote.ahk: Fallback summation requires positive input tokens.
findings.silent_failure: Completion tokens are present but total_tokens is0 and downstream totals omit them.
findings.regression_test: Expect total10 for all three formats with zero input and positive output.

findings.title: UTF-16 BOM alone is accepted as a valid PAC script
findings.reproduction: Judge HTTP200 body FF FE, FE FF or FF FE0000.
findings.root_cause: NetworkCheck_JudgePac in static/ergopti_plus/windows/ui/field_check/network_check.ahk: The UTF-16 BOM branch returns success without decoding or checking the PAC function.
findings.silent_failure: Diagnostics claim a valid PAC and FindProxyForURL despite absent script; the Lua sibling shares this defect.
findings.regression_test: Accept real UTF-16LE/BE PAC scripts; reject BOM-only, odd byte counts, invalid Unicode and content without the function.

findings.title: Update result survives a superseding request
findings.reproduction: Result A enters logging; close A and begin B before logging returns.
findings.root_cause: static/ergopti_plus/windows/ui/update_check/init.ahk:UpdateCheck_ShowResult: Request identity is checked before yielding calls but not before presenting the result.
findings.silent_failure: A replaces B or reopens the closed window.
findings.regression_test: Interrupt the actual logging boundary; reject A and retain B checking.

findings.title: A stale successful WebView build overwrites its replacement
findings.reproduction: While WebView creation for A pumps messages, close A and open B; then return A controller.
findings.root_cause: static/ergopti_plus/windows/ui/update_check/init.ahk:_UpdateCheck_Open: Only the failure path rechecks the opening epoch; the successful path publishes global resources unconditionally.
findings.silent_failure: B loses its controller ownership to the old opening stack.
findings.regression_test: Inject reentrant factory completion and require B resources unchanged and A resources retired once.

findings.title: Update window teardown can close one controller twice
findings.reproduction: Controller.Close reenters CloseWindow through a native window event.
findings.root_cause: static/ergopti_plus/windows/ui/update_check/init.ahk:_UpdateCheck_CloseWindow: Owner invalidation and ResetDone happen after the COM call; no reentrant teardown guard exists.
findings.silent_failure: The same controller closes twice and the host can be destroyed before COM closure unwinds.
findings.regression_test: A passive controller reenters on its first Close; require exact-once closure and destruction.

findings.title: An absent Startup directory prevents portable uninstall
findings.reproduction: Unregister startup shortcuts for an absent Startup folder during an authorized executable removal.
findings.root_cause: static/ergopti_plus/windows/vendor/ergopti_uninstall.ps1:Remove-ErgoptiStartupShortcuts: Get-ChildItem enumerates an optional directory unconditionally under ErrorActionPreference Stop.
findings.silent_failure: The application has exited but recycling never runs.
findings.regression_test: Execute the removal transaction with an absent private folder and a recorded recycle callback.

findings.title: Crash reports confuse process and OS architecture
findings.reproduction: Run the crash worker as PowerShell32 on Windows64.
findings.root_cause: static/ergopti_plus/windows/vendor/ergopti_crash_worker.ps1:architecture enrichment: The worker replaces reliable snapshot os_arch with PROCESSOR_ARCHITECTURE, which describes its own process.
findings.silent_failure: The report says OS x86 although Windows is64-bit.
findings.regression_test: Execute a WOW64 worker with an OS64 snapshot and assert OS architecture remains64-bit.

findings.title: Final file admission can overwrite a concurrent edit
findings.reproduction: Read old as Expected; the final admission writes concurrent and returns1; request replacement.
findings.root_cause: static/ergopti_plus/windows/adapters/file_system.ahk:_FSPublishIfUnchanged: Source equality is checked only before staging and before the reentrant logical admission.
findings.silent_failure: The publication reports success and replaces concurrent.
findings.regression_test: Invoke the actual admitted publisher with a source-mutating admission; require refusal, preserved edit and no stage.

findings.title: Segmented replay keeps the last duplicate within a frame
findings.reproduction: Put two INSERT OR IGNORE batches for the same (device_id,id), first with first.exe and then later.exe, inside one executable frame. One-pass replay keeps first.exe; the segmented first-wins trigger keeps later.exe.
findings.root_cause: static/ergopti_plus/windows/modules/keystats/keystats_reader_rebuild.ahk:_KLR_RebuildInstallFirstWins deletes every conflicting row, assuming every incoming insert is older. A frame executes its own statements forward, so this is false inside the frame.
findings.silent_failure: The existing first-copy regression intentionally uses a small frame size that separates the copies. Wrong survivors change event dates and derived aggregates without a SQL error.
findings.regression_test: Run the existing one-pass-versus-segmented fingerprint fixture with a frame large enough for both copies; retain the small-frame test and check duplicates inside one transaction.

findings.title: A private source title is lost before app-switch filtering
findings.reproduction: Leave a browser window titled Fixture (Private Browsing) for a public application, with private-browsing filtering enabled and the browser not disabled by process name.
findings.root_cause: static/ergopti_plus/windows/modules/keystats/keystats.ahk:KL_LogAppSwitch: The app-switch row retains only prev_app, and the central filter receives no source title.
findings.silent_failure: Live focus names the public destination, so private source application and duration are queued.
findings.regression_test: Use genuine focus, context and append owners, retaining public history; assert no private switch row and no persisted source title.

findings.title: Keep-awake mixes client and physical mouse coordinates
findings.reproduction: Enable keep-awake with Mouse CoordMode Client and a window offset from the screen origin.
findings.root_cause: static/ergopti_plus/windows/modules/shortcuts/win.ahk:StartActivitySimulation, AwakeCheckMouseMoved, SimulateActivity: MouseGetPos uses the thread coordinate mode while MCSetPos always uses physical screen pixels.
findings.silent_failure: The jitter and return can jump away from the physical origin and self-cancel.
findings.regression_test: Use an offset window and Client, Window and Screen modes; record passive physical writes and assert origin-relative bounds.

findings.title: Binary registry methods violate their Buffer contract
findings.reproduction: Write native REG_BINARY hexadecimal00A9FF77 and call Reg_ReadBinary; then attempt Reg_WriteBinary with a four-byte Buffer.
findings.root_cause: static/ergopti_plus/windows/infra/registry.ahk:Reg_ReadBinary and Reg_WriteBinary: AutoHotkey native registry calls exchange hexadecimal strings; the wrappers promise Buffers but omit encoding and decoding.
findings.silent_failure: Reads return a String and Buffer writes fail. No current production caller was found, so impact is the public adapter API.
findings.regression_test: Round-trip exact NUL, A9, FF and77 bytes under a private HKCU key, include an empty buffer and clean up in finally.

findings.title: Hardware diagnostics label ARM64 as x64
findings.reproduction: Run AutoHotkey x64 emulated on Windows ARM64 and collect diagnostics.
findings.root_cause: static/ergopti_plus/windows/ui/healthcheck/helpers.ahk:_HealthCheck_Hardware and infra/diagnostic_snapshot.ahk:DiagSnapshot_Collect: A_Is64bitOS is converted to x64, although it expresses width rather than native machine architecture.
findings.silent_failure: Both diagnostic collectors label the ARM64 host x64.
findings.regression_test: Use a native architecture port and test machine ARM64 with process x64, native x64, and supported x86.

findings.title: PAC diagnostics accept an incorrectly cased entry point
findings.reproduction: Judge HTTP200 body function findproxyforurl(){return 'DIRECT';}, then repeat mixed and upper case variants.
findings.root_cause: static/ergopti_plus/windows/ui/field_check/network_check.ahk:NetworkCheck_JudgePac and ui/healthcheck/probes.ahk:_HC_PacAnswer use the default case-insensitive InStr search. JavaScript and the shared Lua judge require the exact FindProxyForURL identifier.
findings.silent_failure: Windows reports a valid PAC even though its required entry point is absent.
findings.regression_test: Require rejection of lower, upper and mixed case variants in both Windows judges; retain exact-case positive controls.

findings.title: Revoked input still updates ROI after ergonomic publication
findings.reproduction: Type hello, then deliver a space through the genuine hook with its ergonomic callback pausing capture, invalidating the capture generation or changing the focus generation.
findings.root_cause: static/ergopti_plus/windows/modules/keystats/keystats_hook.ahk:_KL_Hook_CommitInput does not revalidate its arrival after ErgoFn.Call before dispatching the ROI sink.
findings.silent_failure: An arrival revoked during the ergonomic callout still clears the current ROI word and increments its candidate count.
findings.regression_test: Use the genuine hook and ROI owners in the isolated keys fixture; revoke through the official ergonomic callback port and require the ROI seed and WPM count to remain unchanged. This qualifies the explicit callout boundary, not atomicity of the whole ROI pipeline.

findings.title: Multi-character InputHook payloads bypass ROI boundaries and bounds
findings.reproduction: Through the genuine hook, append native documented dead-key payload ^z after 63 a characters, then a space. Separately deliver ^.world followed by a space in one callback after hello.
findings.root_cause: static/ergopti_plus/windows/modules/keystats/keystats_trigger_roi.ahk:KL_Roi_OnChar treats its complete callback payload as one character. InputHook.OnChar can deliver multiple characters after an unsuccessful dead-key composition, and a Unicode codepoint can occupy two UTF-16 units.
findings.silent_failure: A candidate exceeds the 64-unit storage bound, or delimiters inside the callback are embedded in a combined word rather than separating words.
findings.regression_test: Use genuine hook and ROI owners to reject a 63-unit prefix plus a two-unit payload or surrogate pair, then assert separate candidates for a callback with an internal delimiter. Native payload shape is documented by AutoHotkey InputHook.OnChar; Windows execution remains pending.

findings.title: Session lifecycle requires a key clock retired by synthetic input
findings.reproduction: Use the existing genuine callback sequence from _KLF_Synthetic, which retains accepted activity1000 but retires KLHook.last_tick to0. Before another manual key, expire the idle timer or request session reset.
findings.root_cause: static/ergopti_plus/windows/modules/keystats/keystats_watchers.ahk:KL_Watchers_IdleTick returns on the retired key clock despite computing the valid accepted boundary. modules/keystats/keystats_collection.ahk:KL_ResetSession forwards the same zero sentinel to the genuine closer instead of considering last_authorized_tick.
findings.silent_failure: An abandoned session never expires until another manual key; explicit reset can throw ValueError when elapsed time is computed from a positive session start to zero.
findings.regression_test: Run genuine capture, synthesis, idle, pointer and session-close owners against the recording append boundary. Cover idle expiry, reset, pointer activity extending reset, and a session legitimately starting at tick zero. Preserve the key clock sentinel for the next manual key's delay.

findings.title: A retired keep-awake keyboard callback stops its successor
findings.reproduction: Start keep-awake A and retain its genuine InputHook, stop A, start B, then deliver the queued callback AwakeCancelOnKeypress(HookA,0x41,0x1E).
findings.root_cause: static/ergopti_plus/windows/modules/shortcuts/win.ahk:AwakeCancelOnKeypress checks the callback type and active flag but never compares the supplied InputHook to the current AwakeInputHook owner.
findings.silent_failure: A delayed callback from the stopped observer cancels the newly activated session B.
findings.regression_test: Extend the isolated keep-awake native owner fixture with actual Start/Stop and two genuine InputHooks. Controlled old-callback delivery must preserve B; current B delivery must stop B. Position and timers remain passive, without physical mouse displacement.

findings.title: Native model browser hides after a refused model selection
findings.reproduction: Open the native model browser, hold a genuine configuration write lease, select model B and click Pick.
findings.root_cause: static/ergopti_plus/windows/ui/model_browser/init.ahk:_LLM_ModelBrowser_PickRow ignores the transactional Boolean returned by LLM_Menu_SetModel and always hides the browser. The Web sibling closes only after an acknowledged success.
findings.silent_failure: The unchanged model A remains selected but its native browser disappears, presenting the refused operation as finished.
findings.regression_test: Use the genuine native browser construction, actual Pick button, full boot/configuration/menu owners and a real write lease. Require visible UI and unchanged file/RAM after refusal; release the lease and require a durable B selection and hidden UI after retry. AppPicker sibling: run41924556519 proves actual lease and sharing refusals destroy the current native picker and lose checkbox selections; both fail after genuine durable refusal. This variant is retained under this durability/presentation family without increasing the finding count. Corrective outcome ownership is being prepared.

findings.title: Native model selection persists while the driver is paused
findings.reproduction: Open the native model browser before Suspend(true), select B and deliver a genuine Pick button click while still suspended.
findings.root_cause: static/ergopti_plus/windows/ui/model_browser/init.ahk:_LLM_ModelBrowser_PickRow has no pause admission guard. Native GUI callbacks bypass Suspend, and the downstream menu transaction validates schema and leases rather than input pause. The Web sibling explicitly rejects suspended model actions.
findings.silent_failure: A model selection can reach the durable writer and publish new live configuration despite the user's driver pause.
findings.regression_test: Use the genuine native browser, observe its actual WM_COMMAND button event while suspended, and require no transaction/writer entry, unchanged durable/RAM state and visible UI. Resume must not replay the click; a fresh unpaused click must still durably select B.

findings.title: A single model word bypasses parser work and allocation limits
findings.reproduction: Parse a 500-character a buffer and TAIL_CORRECTED containing8000 a characters with NEXT_WORDS suite. This8034-byte answer is below the transport ceiling and still contains only one corrected word. Repeat with an oversized next-word field or raw response.
findings.root_cause: static/ergopti_plus/windows/modules/llm/parser.ahk and _shared/lua/llm/parser.lua bound word counts but not character counts or dynamic-programming grid sizes. Character distance and token substitution consume quadratic work; substitution allocates a full matrix. Tokenization and raw cleanup also expand entire oversized words.
findings.silent_failure: A small admitted server response can stall the message/input thread or allocate excessive memory. The actual Lua baseline takes about2.08 CPU seconds and sampled87MiB for an8KiB answer; no AHK runtime measurement is claimed.
findings.regression_test: Both ports read one canonical policy:4096 UTF-8 bytes per operand and262144 cells per conservative diff grid. Refuse oversized corrections, next words and raw output before expensive helpers, then recheck actual normalized diff operands. Assert inclusive byte/cell boundaries and multibyte accounting on Windows; retain all32 shared physical golden vectors. Six real Lua cases pass after the audited baseline fails the oversized-word refusal.

findings.title: Native environment overrides accept an embedded NUL value
findings.reproduction: Build an environment from Map(ERGOPTI_PROBE, keep plus Chr(0) plus drop). The actual Map value preserves its complete length but the native environment uses NUL as its entry delimiter.
findings.root_cause: static/ergopti_plus/windows/adapters/shell_runner.ahk:ShellRunner_BuildEnvironment validates String types but does not refuse NUL before serializing overrides into a launchable NUL-delimited Unicode block.
findings.silent_failure: The child cannot receive the requested complete value and instead sees a shortened value or malformed block. Arbitrary variable injection or execution has not been measured. Ordinary Map keys truncate NUL before enumeration, so that earlier candidate is explicitly not claimed.
findings.regression_test: After actual Map construction, authenticate its retained NUL value and require ValueError for leading, middle and trailing positions. A real native child control verifies exact Unicode, spaces and equals, empty-entry encoding, case-insensitive replacement and an unchanged parent environment.

findings.title: Crash reports count logical processors from only the first socket
findings.reproduction: Collect CPU diagnostics from two Win32_Processor instances reporting8 and12 logical processors. The worker and legacy fallback report8 instead of the machine total20.
findings.root_cause: static/ergopti_plus/windows/vendor/ergopti_crash_worker.ps1 selects the first CIM processor; modules/diagnostics/crash_reporter.ahk:_CrashReport_SysInfo likewise reads only the first WMI instance. NumberOfLogicalProcessors describes its current processor instance, not every socket.
findings.silent_failure: Multi-socket crash reports understate machine CPU capacity. The first model name remains a label; the logical processor count must aggregate all instances.
findings.regression_test: The real isolated worker's existing CIM boundary now returns two heterogeneous8+12 sockets and requires20. The legacy aggregation helper tests the same total, first-name preservation, single socket and explicit rejection of empty or incomplete processor observations. Native Windows execution remains pending.

findings.title: Cold locale loads accept stale same-second translation caches
findings.reproduction: Publish a complete TSV containing before, replace its authoritative JSON with after, set both modification times to the same second, clear the active cache identity and load the locale.
findings.root_cause: _I18nTsvIsFresh in static/ergopti_plus/windows/infra/locale.ahk accepts timestamp equality despite FileGetTime exposing only whole seconds. On a cold load no prior source hash invalidates the stale complete cache.
findings.silent_failure: The old translation is served and associated with the new JSON hash, so subsequent identity reuse can retain stale text.
findings.regression_test: The reachable test_i18n.ahk cold-load regression uses real durable JSON writes, the real TSV publisher and identical native file timestamps; it asserts refreshed memory and disk values, plus a strictly-newer positive fast-path control. Native Windows execution is pending; the pre-fix failure is source-derived.

findings.title: Automatic native ListView sorting shifts the active model selection
findings.reproduction: Open the native catalogue with Qwen3.5-9B active. Its numeric parameter ordering inserts Qwen3.5-27B later, but lexical automatic insertion places 27B before 9B and moves the remembered active row.
findings.root_cause: _LLM_ModelBrowser_Build in static/ergopti_plus/windows/ui/model_browser/init.ahk enables native Sort while _LLM_ModelBrowser_RefreshRows records the active insertion index before all later rows are inserted. Native lexical sorting invalidates both the intended parameter ordering and that index.
findings.silent_failure: The highlighted row can designate a different model, so accepting the initial selection may unexpectedly change the configured model.
findings.regression_test: Extend the reachable model-browser-close-pause-owner native child with native-sort: genuine boot and catalogue, real Gui/ListView construction, active row identity and 9B-before-27B assertions after construction, refresh, filtering and filter removal; no-match and durable-no-write controls. Native Windows execution is pending; pre-fix failure is source-derived.

findings.title: Token exchange throttling and timeouts are reported as invalid API keys
findings.reproduction: Return HTTP 429 or 408 with temporarily_unavailable from the managed access-token exchange used by an API-entry validation.
findings.root_cause: _LLM_TokenExchange_OnAnswer in static/ergopti_plus/windows/modules/llm/api_token_exchange.ahk labels every 4xx response key_refused. _LLMRemote_ReadyOnAccess consequently rewrites a throttling or timeout response to HTTP 401 and the menu selects the invalid-key diagnosis.
findings.silent_failure: A valid stored credential is blamed for transient service or endpoint failures; the actual diagnostic status disappears from validation.
findings.regression_test: Eleven reachable owner-level tests retain 400/401/403 authentication refusals and replay 404/405/408/413/429/503 through genuine exchange settlement, retained retry backoff and waiter reuse; 408/429 additionally exercise actual remote readiness and menu failure classification. Existing OAuth 400 and 401 authentication controls remain. Transport is a declared passive PostFn port; native AHK execution is pending.

findings.title: Log openers report no errors before buffered warnings reach disk
findings.reproduction: Emit a real warning with the periodic logger flush not yet delivered, then immediately invoke the errors-log action; alternatively open the main log while that warning is still buffered.
findings.root_cause: LogOpeners_OpenTodayErrors in static/ergopti_plus/windows/ui/log_openers.ahk checks FileExist without first settling the real logger queues. Warnings are intentionally buffered until the periodic flush. The main-log sibling likewise opens a stale disk snapshot. A flush return alone is insufficient because refused appends are requeued.
findings.silent_failure: The UI says no errors today despite an accepted warning, or opens a file missing the latest diagnostic. A locked sink can produce the same false answer unless retained delivery debt is checked.
findings.regression_test: Six isolated owned native logger children cover main/errors, genuine native sharing denial with retained exactly-once retry, and an explicitly controlled busy-owner observation. Launch reads the genuine file at the action boundary and requires the warning; notification must remain unused. Existing resolver action tests isolate their own logger queues. Native Windows execution is pending; the original failure is source-derived.

findings.title: Deferred tap-copy retries survive suspend and can overwrite successor ownership
findings.reproduction: Start a tap-copy check, enter native Suspend and the production remap teardown, resume before the retained 300 ms callback, then deliver that old callback with an unchanged clipboard counter. Also start a newer copy inside the counter or retry sender of an older check.
findings.root_cause: TapCopyCheckStop in static/ergopti_plus/windows/platform/remap/constants.ahk was never reached by production cleanup. The timer checked only the instantaneous suspended flag. Producer and timer continuations also mutated the global pending record after counter, sender or logger callouts without revalidating their exact generation.
findings.silent_failure: An old Ctrl+C may be injected into the resumed context, or an obsolete check may clear a newer copy and issue its stale failure notification.
findings.regression_test: Seven reachable tap-copy-owner cases invoke the genuine suspend-owned remap drain with private empty modifier ledgers, native Suspend/resume and retained timer delivery; producer/counter/retry/logger callouts revoke or replace ownership and assert zero stale sends/notices plus successor timer preservation. Counter/timer/send/notice are explicit passive ports. Existing five copy verification controls remain. Native Windows execution is pending; pre-fix failure is source-derived.

findings.title: Managed GET redirects can forward a caller body to another origin
findings.reproduction: Send a nonempty body through the exposed managed GET adapter to an owned origin returning HTTP 301, 302, 307 or 308 to a different origin. The redirect loop strips headers but forwards the staged body.
findings.root_cause: ergopti_managed_http_worker.ps1 in static/ergopti_plus/windows/vendor checks only whether a cross-origin method differs from GET. It does not inspect the current SendBody state and actual body length, while the genuine WinHTTP transport sends bodies independently of the method.
findings.silent_failure: The adapter violates its explicit cross-origin payload policy by contacting the second origin with the original GET body. No current production caller sending a nonempty GET body was found; this is an exposed adapter-contract defect, not an observed end-user disclosure.
findings.regression_test: A reachable managed-redirect-body-owner AHK case launches the genuine worker with its real admission handshake and WinHTTP engine against two owned loopback peers. Twelve native controls require denial before target contact, empty-GET and 303 controls, same-origin body preservation, and existing POST denial. Native peers record only body lengths and SHA256 digests. The original raw transport controls remain. Native Windows execution is pending.

findings.title: Retired tap-hold frames can release or overwrite a resumed gesture
findings.reproduction: Acquire a real immediate modifier, enter native Suspend and genuine remap teardown, resume and acquire the same modifier again before the old KeyWait frame returns. The retired frame consumes the new reference. The native fail-before replay41889866195 at7ee17bcef5076c4238a2e090cf41cb6d70ccf90b reports the exact missing-successor-ledger assertion.
findings.root_cause: The remap owner protocol in platform/remap/constants.ahk identifies release authority only by key name. Native Suspend leaves waiting frames alive. A late finally therefore consumes a new reference, while paired Tab-up/finally paths can consume twice in the same epoch. Companion AltGr handback, roll decisions and layer teardown carry similarly unqualified identity across callouts. OneShotShift additionally releases its SIHO capture before activation without retaining the gesture epoch through subsequent special-result emission.
findings.silent_failure: A held Ctrl/Alt/Shift can be released under another gesture or a newly physical-held key; an old frame may remove successor metadata or dispatch an obsolete tap after resume.
findings.regression_test: Fourteen reachable synthetic-owner cases drive the genuine modifier, Tab, AltGr, rollover and navigation-layer owners with native Suspend/resume and the real lifecycle drain. Passive input, clock and wait ports expose release receipts, debt, physical observations and exact successor preservation without typing into the desktop. Two additional dispatch cases use the genuine logger test sink to revoke during the actual cancellation log and preserve resumed tracking. Native qualification is recorded separately with exact revisions. Two further one-shot rearm activation cases use the real SIHO owner, real empty-ledger teardown and a native timer during the activation I/O port. Native run41901785093 atafc1dd3 confirms both old-result emissions before the fix, with the unchanged special-result control passing. The successor variant preserves an independently admitted SIHO hook. These variants remain one gesture-authority finding.

findings.title: A raced physical modifier restoration loses its failed balancing release
findings.reproduction: On a Kana layout, run the genuine hotstring output lift around a delivered user-held AltGr. Release the physical key immediately after its synthetic restoration Down succeeds, then refuse the compensating Up. Native run41895428966 atd17134a05d7dcea57f92ff0dbf2b6bc3e7f80540 reproduces the missing pending-release assertion in both controls, individually and reversed.
findings.root_cause: TapHoldRestoreLiftedKey in platform/remap/constants.ahk directly sends a compensating Up after detecting a physical release racing its successful scalar re-press. Unlike failed Array-acquisition rollback, this independent producer never transfers the proven Down to the release-pending ledger when that Up fails.
findings.silent_failure: The restored modifier can remain logically down after the user lets go. Suspend or shutdown reports no outstanding key and never retries the missing balancing Up.
findings.regression_test: Two reachable raced-repress-release-debt cases run the actual hotstring lift/restore path on the production Kana key mapping with an explicit passive transport and physical-state observations. They distinguish successful delivery from refused attempts, require retained debt through refused real lifecycle cleanup, and verify subsequent cleanup or a fresh owner repairs it before further acquisition. Native fail-before proof is retained; post-fix native execution remains pending.

findings.title: Personal file publication can outlive its final editor or pause authorization
findings.reproduction: At the genuine native replacement cutpoint after existing admission checks, close the real personal-hotstring editor, suspend the driver, release the exact path lease, relocate the configured path, or retire the captured information editor/resident map. Native run41897311070 at70481abbcdfc32060a2424b2a17b48fd19ac87ca passed the three live controls and reproduced all ten stale replacements, individually and reversed.
findings.root_cause: _PersonalTomlWriteAtomic and _PersonalInfoReplaceUnchanged in infra/hotstrings/personal_toml_io.ahk restore interruption after their pure authority checks, then invoke unguarded FSAtomicMoveReplace. The final native producer never resamples the revocable facts. Metadata patches also omit their already-issued owner from that final boundary.
findings.silent_failure: A cancelled or paused save can still replace the personal file and publish a stale intention after the editor or path authority has retired. This differs from AHK-014 external source-byte mutation: the violated facts here are in-process owner, pause, configured identity and session authority.
findings.regression_test: Thirteen reachable personal native final admission cases use real private files, durable stages, actual GUI/source and lease owners, a declared interruptible internal cutpoint, and the genuine native rename producer. Three controls prove actual successful replacement; ten withdrawal variants require original target bytes, no publication and cleaned stage. Existing arbitrary two-argument ReplaceFn ports stay outside Critical. The fixed native branch uses FSConfigAtomicMoveReplace with a pure final guard; external-process filesystem compare-and-swap is outside this guarantee. Post-fix native qualification is pending.

findings.title: Walker composite keys merge distinct literal application and token values
findings.reproduction: Push literal tokens a and a+NUL+b through the genuine Windows n-gram producer, or push tuples (day,A+Chr1+B,C) and (day,A,B+Chr1+C), then flush through the actual SQL builder to native SQLite. Native run41896696315 atbe1e23b2047ebd958ed2d147c2a616c493c22a61 reproduces all three producer/replay probes alone and reversed: expected3 rows become2; genuine typing replay expected2 becomes1.
findings.root_cause: Windows walker constructors concatenate unescaped fields using Chr1 and then store that text in AutoHotkey Maps, whose string keys end at NUL. N-gram SQL reconstructs original field values by splitting the already ambiguous key. Other projection and per-application context constructors share that identity assumption.
findings.silent_failure: Accepted replay data silently combines independent counts and delays and can persist truncated or reassigned application/token values. This concerns supported literal replay/JSON values; no physical-keyboard NUL sequence is claimed.
findings.regression_test: Three native fail-before probes retain literal SQL hex(app)/hex(token), repeated additive controls and a genuine typing replay. The fix escapes only internal tuple fields and preserves raw row values for SQL. Five further cases cover shared array byte vectors, real JSON context roundtrip and legacy retirement, cache17 refusal, checkpoint3 restart and obsolete stage cleanup. Existing aggregation, distribution merge, rollover and current checkpoint controls remain. Cache18/checkpoint4 force reconstruction without changing raw ledgers or persisted token encoding2. Scope is Windows: the separately measured shared Lua Chr1 collision and Linux aggregate-history migration remain open outside this OS correction; no Lua source is changed. Post-fix native qualification is pending.

findings.title: Refused native entry edits leave a ghost editor model and block retry
findings.reproduction: Use the actual native personal editor and a real read-shared file handle denying write/delete. Click Add, Delete or Save through BM_CLICK. The native rename refuses, but the mutable editor model already contains the edit while the file and ListView retain their old values. Native run41900510051 at7306179ef66936fd43660b7382c65d702d0f1cc0 reproduces the exact unchanged-model failures for all three operations, alone and reversed, plus section/legacy variants.
findings.root_cause: _AddEntry, _SaveEntry and _DeleteEntry in ui/personal_toml_editor.ahk mutate _PersonalEditorData before _SaveData obtains the durable/live transaction receipt. Failure never restores model/ListView agreement. A simple rollback would lose overlapping DEFERRED snapshots, so complete detached candidates and exact completion ownership are required.
findings.silent_failure: An invisible non-durable added entry blocks its own retry as a duplicate. A refused deletion leaves old native row indices pointing into a different model, so a later retry can address another entry. Deferred and section publications must preserve their visible unsaved drafts without stale completion effects.
findings.regression_test: Ten reachable personal-entry-receipts cases use real GUI controls, native button messages, a real sharing-denial handle and unlocked same-form retry. They also drive actual coalesced publication, terminal deferred failure and complete-snapshot recovery, dropdown/section changes and the legacy save entry point. The fix installs detached candidates only after immediate success or explicit DEFERRED admission, keeps RAM and rows coherent, and fences completions by source/cohort/sequence. Existing modal and live transaction controls remain; native post-fix qualification is measured. Native post-fix evidence: run41902865547 passed all 71 selected UI business cases individually and reversed; run41907002685 at14c9580 additionally passed the five repaired structural/isolation adapters inside its green 66-case cohort.

findings.title: Cold hotstring caches can register rules from retired or replaced sources
findings.reproduction: Publish a genuine cache, remove its authoritative bundled TOML, or edit that TOML after actual BuildRows but before actual WriteTsv. Alternatively build while a real scanned extension binds autocorrection, then remove that extension and route. Native run41903520217 atdd8ee6ae63db99448f548466b3fbfba89389e8d0 passed the unchanged live control and reproduced all three ghost registrations through the real Ensure/category registrar, individually and reversed.
findings.root_cause: infra/hotstrings/hotstrings_cache.ahk treats later TSV timestamps as source identity, skips missing dependencies, and derives cache paths from an effective resolver that can point at extensions. The TSV has no record of the canonical index image actually consumed, source paths/presence or content hashes. The initial rebuilt RAM projection also needs admission after the writer and its yielding diagnostics.
findings.silent_failure: Removed or replaced rules become active native triggers on a cold load. A cache can silently retain extension data after its source is gone, or bless older parsed content with a newer publication timestamp.
findings.regression_test: Four native fail-before cases use real temporary canonical sources, the actual index memo, real extension scan/routing and actual HSE registration. The single-file TSV fix records consumed index/source provenance plus closed row/count/payload proof and validates the exact parsed candidate. Physical bundled resolution is separate from adopted extension routes. Two additional initial-publication cases use real stage sharing denial and the genuine logger sink to edit a category or index after BuildRows. Rebuilt RAM snapshots are checked after writer callouts, retried at most twice and otherwise refused with cleared maps. Valid TOML loading still works when cache writes fail. Three existing freshness owners now publish genuine source-backed fixtures. Native post-fix qualification is measured; no cold-load performance measurement or filesystem-wide external CAS is claimed. Native post-fix evidence: run41907002685 at14c9580 passed all 66 selected cache/editor cases individually and reversed, the complete production compile and hotstring E2E90/90; full-suite qualification remains false.

findings.title: Raw body retries bypass current access-token preparation
findings.reproduction: Prepare an original resolved record through the genuine cached-access owner, then renew or expire its token slot before calling RawPost. Native run41904156246 ate26726d4ca7ea2d98dd2370648ca15f1dcc5dbf0 passes the fresh control but publishes Bearer old-token instead of the actual renewed new-token. Four expired-slot variants also reach a transport before starting exchange. All failures reproduce individually and reversed.
findings.root_cause: LLM_RemotePostBody_Async in modules/llm/api_remote.ahk reserves its request then dispatches the retained Resolved.Token directly. Generate calls _LLMRemote_NeedsAccess and _LLMRemote_WithAccess, but thinking retries and screen-reading bodies using RawPost omit that preparation. NeedsAccess must be called even when it returns false because it refreshes the retained Token from the current slot.
findings.silent_failure: A later body can carry an expired or superseded credential and receive an avoidable authentication refusal despite a valid current cached access token or available refresh.
findings.regression_test: Six token-rawpost-owner cases run the actual resolver, original access preparation, token engine, RawPost reservation, managed facade and transport.json serializer. Only exchange HTTP and process spawning use existing explicitly controlled I/O ports; this is no native wire-success claim. The actual published header must use current access; expired slots await exchange under the same id, clock and deadline. Cancellation, elapsed deadline and native pause must prevent dispatch. The optional final TransportPort defaults to zero and forwards the preexisting downstream test boundary without changing current callers. Native fail-before proof is measured; native post-fix qualification is measured. Native post-fix: run41908552045 at36e7a60 passed all 15 selected cases individually and reversed and the complete production compile; E2E families were not selected.

findings.title: Managed HTTP failures discard the provider classification and message
findings.reproduction: Native loopback run41907263356 at8a5643a passes the real HTTP200 completion control. The HTTP400 peer receives exactly one POST and returns owned-classification-refusal, but the genuine callback receives transport and an empty server_message rather than provider_error and the actual refusal. The same failure occurs individually and reversed.
findings.root_cause: _LLMRemote_PollRequest classifies the actual managed response then replaces reason and server_message with hard-coded transport and an empty string when terminal_ok is false. The curl consumer already forwards these classifier fields.
findings.silent_failure: Provider refusals lose their explanation and cannot reach existing request-field retry decisions; callers instead receive an inaccurate transport failure.
findings.regression_test: Two managed-http-classification cases use the actual Generate path, native owned loopback peer, real managed HTTP body and neutral callback collectors. The genuine network host is initialized and restored under an exclusive fixture scope. HTTP200 must complete once; HTTP400 must preserve the actual classifier reason, exact server message and retained network report. Native fail-before measured; post-fix qualification measured. Native post-fix: both actual HTTP classification cases passed individually and reversed in run41908674329 at944d513; the mixed four-case cohort remains red only for the independently measured AHK-044.

findings.title: Cancelled API tests can dispatch a thinking-field retry after losing their original reservation
findings.reproduction: Native run41908674329 at944d513 passes the two-POST thinking-retry control. At the actual refusal logger cutpoint the original reservation is already retired; cancel the genuine progress window there. Its owner and window retire, but a new second reservation and second native HTTP POST still appear. The exact expected1/observed2 failure reproduces individually and reversed.
findings.root_cause: The Menu API test supplies callbacks and a request kind to Generate without its supported CurrentFn authority. CancelAsync(original) cannot find a retry that has not yet been reserved, so the retry sender is admitted after the progress owner is gone.
findings.silent_failure: Clicking Cancel can still send another prompt to the provider after the native progress window closes and the auxiliary test owner is retired.
findings.regression_test: Two api-thinking-retry-owner cases drive the actual native Menu progress GUI, genuine Generate/managed HTTP and an owned loopback peer. A real logger sink cancels exactly between original retirement and retry admission; the positive control must issue two requests and settle successfully, while cancellation must leave one request, no retry link and no retired UI publication. The fix binds the exact progress owner through the existing Generate CurrentFn argument. Native fail-before measured; post-fix qualification measured in run41909512571 ata6373a4: both cases passed individually and reversed, with two requests for the positive control and one request for cancellation. The mixed cohort remains red for AHK-046/AHK-047.

findings.title: Queued key-combination chords replay input during native pause
findings.reproduction: Native run41908766133 atb4eff5c passes both unpaused controls. Suspending before real SetTimer delivery still emits the waiting key (expected0/observed1) or the queued scan (expected1/observed2). Both failures repeat individually and reversed.
findings.root_cause: KeyCombinationChordTick treats suspension as a reason to flush a waiting key, and KeyCombinationChordDrain sends its retained queue without pause admission. Neither batch retains lifecycle authority, so resume before delivery and reentrant successor callbacks also require fencing.
findings.silent_failure: The paused driver can inject a key it retained before pause. A retired callback can also act on a newly admitted waiting or queued batch after lifecycle teardown and resume.
findings.regression_test: Four chord-native-pause cases deliver real native poll/drain timers around Suspend; production chord policy and engine remain genuine while keyboard transport is observed through its existing recorder. Two positive controls prove actual replay; two paused cases must discard unsent work and keep it retired after resume. No balancing-Up change or physical keyboard proof is claimed. Native fail-before measured; The fix retains an exact batch owner from the existing synthetic lifecycle epoch, retires unsent state, checks callback identity and admits each short send atomically under Critical. Four additional regressions cover pause/resume before timer delivery and genuine held-state/logger callouts that admit a successor. Busy reads in roll admission also retire stale batches. Arbitrary actions remain outside Critical. Native post-fix qualification is measured. Native post-fix: run41910772341 atf7e7b2f passed all21 selected chord cases and21 adjacent roll cases individually and reversed, plus full production compile.

findings.title: Clipboard native monotonic ages are truncated into DWORD aliases
findings.reproduction: Native run41909512571 ata6373a4 passes the ordinary clock control but both one-era and two-era cases fail the full copy-age assertion, individually and reversed. Genuine accepted copy/paste producers own the timestamps; only the actual paste clock observation is bound to a later native64 value.
findings.root_cause: KL_Clip_OnPaste computes native A_TickCount differences with an explicit UInt32 mask for copy_lag_ms and retained paste_ticks. These origins are full-width monotonic ticks rather than clipboard sequence DWORDs. Retained old copy/burst state can therefore alias recent activity after 2^32 milliseconds.
findings.silent_failure: Long-lived retained clipboard metadata reports a short copy age and can turn ancient pastes into a fresh burst after roughly49.7 days or a multiple thereof.
findings.regression_test: Three clipboard-paste-native64 cases use actual accepted copy/paste producers, native privacy/context/queue owners and an isolated existing child. Only the unique current paste-clock read is bound; no timestamp state is assigned. Ordinary activity, one/two DWORD eras and subsequent fresh activity must preserve full lag and burst retirement. TickElapsed64 replaces the two masks without changing copy provenance. Native fail-before measured; post-fix measured. No49-day native uptime is claimed. Native post-fix: all three native64 clock cases passed individually and reversed in run41910772341 atf7e7b2f.

findings.title: A late token answer can mark an expired readiness request successful
findings.reproduction: Native run41909512571 ata6373a4 passes the timely token answer. A genuine answer timer begins while the request owner is current and its clock live, then crosses the unchanged96ms deadline under Critical before delivering the actual token answer. Readiness returns true instead of false, individually and reversed.
findings.root_cause: _LLMRemote_ReadyOnAccess checks auxiliary identity but omits the stored absolute whole-request deadline. For a nonlisting request it publishes true immediately after successful token preparation even if the due deadline timer has not yet run.
findings.silent_failure: Save-time credential validation can report success after its total request budget expired, depending on native callback delivery order. The shared usable token may correctly remain cached while the expired individual validation must fail.
findings.regression_test: Two token-ready-deadline cases run public readiness and the genuine token engine through the existing passive exchange HTTP port, with actual AHK timer delivery. The late reply crosses the original real budget; neither origin nor duration is moved. Timely control, current-owner checks, exact one-result receipt and preserved token cache distinguish authority from credential lifetime. The narrow fix checks the original deadline in ReadyOnAccess. Native fail-before measured; post-fix measured. macOS/Linux token readiness continues through a request rather than this Windows-only nonlisting shortcut. Native post-fix: both real timer deadline cases passed individually and reversed in run41910772341 atf7e7b2f.

findings.title: Clamped hotstring delays lose their persistent relative offset
findings.reproduction: Native run41910772341 atf7e7b2f passes the unclipped, unlimited and explicit replacement controls. Three cases fail individually and reversed: rebasing a clamped offset disagrees with a genuine reload; an unrelated colour save changes the source offset; returning the base after an intermediate clamp fails to restore the original effective delay.
findings.root_cause: _HotstringsRecordApplyBase clears PendingOffset after storing only the clamped effective Delay. Rebase and serialisation later reconstruct the offset from this lossy projection, while transaction clones also omit the original finite intent. The shared delay corpus explicitly requires retaining the original offset when the effect clamps.
findings.silent_failure: Changing a base delay or saving an unrelated colour silently changes a user’s configured timing intention, both in the live projection and on disk.
findings.regression_test: Six HotstringsConfig persistent offset cases use real TOML, the canonical typed decoder, production parser/projection/resolver, actual public colour and delay writers and fresh reload comparisons. The fix retains StoredOffset through projection and detached transaction clones; explicit delay edits replace it and clears retire it. Category and section paths are checked. Native fail-before measured; post-fix qualification measured. Shared Lua already preserves the offset in its rung and computes clamping only in projection. Native run41912869071 ate4e5e62 passed all six new and ten adjacent override cases individually and reversed; production compile, hotstring E2E90/90 and HTTP adapter E2E11/11 passed. The mixed probe cohort does not qualify the complete suite.

findings.title: Finite hotstring offsets override an explicit unlimited delay
findings.reproduction: Native run41910772341 atf7e7b2f passes unlimited-only and offset-only controls but fails both source orders containing delay_unlimited=true and delay_offset=-0.25 at base0.75. The actual valid TOML resolves finite instead of unlimited, individually and reversed.
findings.root_cause: The Windows parser independently admits the two correctly typed leaves, then _HotstringsRecordApplyBase consumes the pending finite offset after Delay has already been set to zero by the explicit unlimited flag. The shared Lua resolver explicitly prioritizes true unlimited. This occurs above the clamp and is distinct from AHK-048.
findings.silent_failure: A valid explicit unlimited setting silently acquires a finite activation deadline, so expansions can be refused contrary to the chosen configuration.
findings.regression_test: Four HotstringsConfig unlimited precedence cases use real typed TOML, the actual parser/base projection/resolver and both category and section scope. Both leaf orders must be unlimited; single-leaf controls preserve finite and unlimited behavior. The fix clears finite projection state and returns when explicit unlimited has already been parsed. No format change. Native fail-before measured; post-fix measured. Native run41912869071 ate4e5e62 passed all four precedence cases individually and reversed; production compile, hotstring E2E90/90 and HTTP adapter E2E11/11 passed. The mixed probe cohort does not qualify the complete suite.

findings.title: The native personal-editor case checkbox does not control exact matching
findings.reproduction: Native run41910772341 atf7e7b2f fails both genuine GUI probes individually and reversed: Add with the case checkbox checked persists strict_case=false; unchecking an existing strictly matched entry preserves strict_case=true after Save. Both use actual BM_CLICK and the durable native writer.
findings.root_cause: _BuildEntry derives is_case_sensitive from the checkbox but derives strict_case from an unrelated hidden argument. Add defaults that argument false and Save supplies the previous entry flag regardless of the current checkbox. The shared editor already maps this checkbox to both producer flags, matching the documented exact-match UI contract.
findings.silent_failure: The checked native editor can still match a differently cased trigger, while unchecking can leave exact matching enabled. The persisted configuration contradicts the visible option.
findings.regression_test: Two real PEER native GUI cases verify durable typed flags and then observe the registry actually published by the real commit through the genuine matcher, without output injection. A detached registry/matcher scope refuses an active prefix watcher, drains its genuine auxiliary timer and restores original state. The obsolete hidden-argument unit oracle becomes a checkbox matrix, and the unused argument is removed. Generic parsing/cache/dispatch preserve the independent flags. Native fail-before measured; post-fix measured. macOS/Linux shared editor producer already implements this mapping. Native run41912869071 ate4e5e62 passed all two native GUI and one checkbox unit cases individually and reversed; production compile, hotstring E2E90/90 and HTTP adapter E2E11/11 passed. The mixed probe cohort does not qualify the complete suite.

findings.title: A token exchange revoked by pause imposes a provider-failure cooldown after resume
findings.reproduction: Run41910983878 atc93908c passes success, HTTP403 and original-deadline controls. Pause after actual managed admission and deliver a late valid token response through the genuine facade. The facade correctly aborts with status0, but after resume the token slot retains retry_at and serves a cached failure: posts remain1 instead of2 and verdicts become2. The same failure reproduces individually and reversed.
findings.root_cause: The managed facade loses the cause of its refusal when it represents pause revocation as an aborted status0 response. The later token polling consumer treats that result as a provider/transport failure and installs the normal60-second backoff. Checking current suspension only cannot distinguish a consumer delivered after resume.
findings.silent_failure: An explicit driver pause creates an artificial provider refusal for subsequent legitimate token requests, delaying normal operation after resume despite no provider authentication failure.
findings.regression_test: Five token-managed-pause cases use genuine Prepare/Begin/Post, managed facade admission and original deadlines, actual token polling timers and native Suspend. Only Job/HTTP process I/O is controlled, not a wire/process-native proof. Success,403 and timeout retain their intended policies; pause and resume-before-Poll require a fresh exchange without cooldown. A narrow facade latch records only an actual pause refusal on a still-active unexpired request, and the internal Answer conveys that fact to token settlement. Secondary cleanup failures remain visible. Native four-case fail-before measured; post-fix qualification measured. Prompt cancellation of a silent server is outside this finding. Native run41912869071 ate4e5e62 passed all five token and14 adjacent managed-owner cases individually and reversed; production compile, hotstring E2E90/90 and HTTP adapter E2E11/11 passed. The mixed probe cohort does not qualify the complete suite.

findings.title: Rollover can delete an unconsumed journal that replaces the checked file
findings.reproduction: Native run41912869071 ate4e5e62 passes the unchanged-file control. In the swap case, real MoveFileExW succeeds while the verified reader remains open, a new today.log is written and its distinct native identity is confirmed. Resume then returns true instead of refusing. Its successful branch executes FileDelete on that replacement path and publishes final rollover state. The failure repeats individually and reversed; the baseline test stops before directly observing the post-return absence.
findings.root_cause: _KL_RolloverResume verifies the original consumed file through a reader that denies write sharing but permits deletion/rename. It then deletes by path, so the verified object and the deleted object can differ. Holding journal logical ownership does not pin an external filesystem replacement.
findings.silent_failure: A concurrent replacement journal containing new events can be deleted even though only its predecessor was consumed and committed, permanently losing those new events.
findings.regression_test: Two actual ingest/prepare/recovery cases use a narrow original I/O cutpoint, real native rename/replacement, actual journal owners, durable receipts and SQLite event verification. The fix clones the original consumed snapshot and uses FSDeleteVerified with a native receipt comparator; final removal marks the exact exclusively verified handle. A replacement must survive unchanged and retain pending recovery/offset; retry remains fenced without duplicate ingestion. The unchanged control must complete. Source-wiring tests retain EOF/prepare/save ordering and now require verified deletion with the original proof. Native fail-before measured; post-fix measured. Native post-fix: run41919871873 at2298478 passed all nine recovery cases and nine adjacent metadata/EOF cases individually and reversed.

findings.title: Sticky modifier capture leaks the original nontext key before its modified replay
findings.reproduction: Native run41912869071 ate4e5e62 passes letter and Enter controls but fails Backspace individually and reversed. A real timer sends Backspace to a verified child-owned Edit while genuine StickyModifier/SIHO captures it: one original WM_KEYDOWN reaches the editor and removes its last character before the passive Ctrl replay is recorded.
findings.root_cause: StickyModifier creates a text-suppressive InputHook but leaves VisibleNonText at its native true default. Ending nontext keys such as Backspace can reach the foreground application before the one-shot owner replays them with its chosen modifiers.
findings.silent_failure: An application receives an unmodified editing/navigation action in addition to the requested sticky shortcut. The raw edit can already change text even if the modified output later refuses, or can make the combined shortcut remove more text than intended.
findings.regression_test: Three sticky-native-nontext cases extract the actual StickyModifier/Names owner and include genuine SIHO. Actual SendEvent input is explicitly opted in and confined to a verified child-owned foreground Edit; TextPressKey alone is passive. Native WM_KEYDOWN, edit content, exact modified output and cleanup must agree. Letter and Enter are native controls, not claimed failing variants; Backspace proves the defect. Setting VisibleNonText=false retains standard modifier visibility under the native InputHook policy. Native fail-before measured; post-fix measured. Native post-fix: all three native nontext/letter controls passed individually and reversed in run41919871873 at2298478.

findings.title: A stale navigation-layer editor can overwrite a newer configuration
findings.reproduction: Native run41912869071 ate4e5e62 opens the actual layer host with sourceA, independently writes valid sourceB, then delivers the old page save through the real SDK bridge and host dispatch. Its receipt records save_entered1, save_returned1, apply_calls1 and newer_bytes_preserved0, individually and reversed. The three adjacent ready-delivery controls pass.
findings.root_cause: The Windows layer editor reads text for the page but retains no source receipt bound to its exact host, epoch, folders and target. GUI Save then uses an explicit unconditional writer, so it can adopt and replace later bytes from another editor.
findings.silent_failure: Saving an unchanged older page erases a newer navigation binding and requests applying that stale content. A retired host must also lose authority to request apply after a successful durable save.
findings.regression_test: The real LRDT host/native GUI, SDK callback, host timer dispatch and canonical corpus drive source-stale plus a fresh-host successful save. The fix captures the offered source once per host and uses the existing lease and admitted unchanged-source publisher; explicit non-GUI Save retains its existing contract. Exact host/epoch/folders/target admission persists through publication and is checked again after success logging before apply. A separate real WM_CLOSE-at-success-log probe observes saved=true/applied=false with zero apply calls. FakeHost save cases become explicitly inert rather than manufacturing consent. Native stale-source fail-before measured; post-fix pending. Linux already retains this opening receipt; the macOS sibling remains outside this Windows correction. Native post-fix run41924556519 at9a8ebad passes the selected regression cases individually and reversed, with full production compile and90/90 native hotstring E2E. HTTP E2E was not selected.

findings.title: Wrap-symbol TOML projection can erase or corrupt valid settings
findings.reproduction: Native run41912869071 ate4e5e62 passes four canonical/quoted/legacy controls. Three annotated valid TOML cases fail individually and reversed: an unrelated accepted AddCustom deletes the original pair after an annotated header; an annotated disabled value is serialized incorrectly; an annotated custom value prevents an otherwise valid save.
findings.root_cause: _WS_Load interprets TOML using exact header strings and greedy double-quote regex captures without canonical lexical handling. Comments can hide a recognized table or enter its value. Literal/multiline strings and invalid recognized types also need a trustworthy typed projection so an incomplete interpretation cannot later be acknowledged as empty configuration.
findings.silent_failure: A routine unrelated wrap-symbol edit can permanently remove a valid custom pair or re-enable/corrupt a disabled symbol. Valid source annotations can also make persistence unusable.
findings.regression_test: Seven inline-comment/quote/legacy cases use real Init, the actual shared catalogue, public AddCustom, independent typed disk decoding and genuine reload. The corrected loader alone uses the existing canonical lexer/decoder, preserves legacy semicolon comments and CSV/default-right behavior, projects into detached state and latches recognized unprojectable data. Writer and transactions are unchanged. Twelve extra spelling/compatibility/type-preservation probes cover the same family without increasing the count. The historical custom-before-disabled metadata test becomes an actual save/reload fixture retaining its original test identity. Native three-case fail-before measured; post-fix measured. Extra grammar variants are coverage, not separate native-confirmed findings. Native post-fix: all35 selected wrap loader, spelling, preservation and transaction controls passed individually and reversed in run41919871873 at2298478.

findings.title: Sorting the native personal-entry list targets a different stored entry
findings.reproduction: Native run41919871873 at2298478 uses the real native constructor, header click, selection and original Save/Delete buttons. Both cases report displayed alpha/form zeta/header_clicks1. Save changes the other stored entry while alpha remains unchanged; Delete leaves alpha present after a different entry was removed. The same failures repeat in reverse.
findings.root_cause: The native personal editor permits automatic header sorting but its form, Save and Delete handlers use the visible row number directly as the TOML entry-array index. Header ordering therefore separates displayed identity from the record mutated. This differs from AHK-031’s initial active-model insertion ordering.
findings.silent_failure: Editing or deleting the selected visible row can mutate another persistent personal expansion. The form and confirmation may also describe the wrong record, rather than the row the user selected.
findings.regression_test: Two personal-native-sort-owner probes use the production public native fallback, a real header HWND click, actual selection and BM_CLICK on the original buttons. Independent durable TOML checks follow the displayed trigger identity and inspect the result before the form assertion. No copied ListView style or fake writer is used. Adding NoSort retains TOML row order; the native editor does not advertise a separate sorting feature. Native fail-before measured; post-fix qualification pending. Native post-fix run41924556519 at9a8ebad passes the selected regression cases individually and reversed, with full production compile and90/90 native hotstring E2E. HTTP E2E was not selected.

findings.title: The click-release watcher stops after three characters while Button Up is still owed
findings.reproduction: Raw native evidence from run41919871873 at2298478 proves Down accepted, two genuine keyboard callbacks with refused Up, then Input=abc/EndReason=Max/InProgress=false on the third character. Sending d returns under the owned Edit target guard, but no further Up is attempted and the final held-debt assertion fails, individually and reversed. The one-character retry control passes. The generic last-observation phase label was initially misread as an acquisition failure; the actual failing assertion is subject.ahk:554 after the next-key observation.
findings.root_cause: GestureStartKeyboardWatcher constructs InputHook("V L3") and describes L3 as an input level. L is a collected-text length limit, so three characters terminate the only shared keyboard observer even when a refused mouse release still needs later retries.
findings.silent_failure: A synthetic held mouse button can remain held after later keyboard input because its recovery observer has already ended. Retaining typed text is unnecessary for a key-down observer.
findings.regression_test: Three gesture-keywatcher-length cases use the actual native hook and callbacks, keyboard injection confined to an explicitly opted-in verified child-owned Edit, and passive mouse I/O. One, three and eight refused-key sequences must retain the same observer, recover at the next allowed Up and pass the complete typed text through. The fix uses V L0 and KeyOpt All NI, preserving MinSendLevel0, notifications and visible input while ignoring text collection. Old pins are adapted; final held-state and cleanup oracles remain strict. Native three-character fail-before measured; long/text-retention coverage and post-fix qualification pending. No physical mouse injection or physical-key claim is made. Native post-fix run41924556519 at9a8ebad passes the selected regression cases individually and reversed, with full production compile and90/90 native hotstring E2E. HTTP E2E was not selected.

findings.title: Day rollover never yields when the journal ends in an incomplete record
findings.reproduction: Native Windows run41919871873 at2298478 executes torn-drain and undelimited-drain through the real journal reader and rollover owner. Both require the bounded one-second rescue timer to revoke initialization; the committed offset stays108. The blank-batch-drain control advances over5001 empty lines and succeeds.
findings.root_cause: KL_DayRollover repeats every successful non-EOF ingest without checking committed byte progress. The reader deliberately preserves an unterminated record, so each iteration revisits the same offset and cannot complete the rollover or yield to the resident writer.
findings.silent_failure: A final partial journal record can trap day rollover in a tight loop. The journal must remain intact until its final delimiter arrives.
findings.regression_test: The three new rollover-state-recovery cases exercise actual files, reader, SQLite ledger and owner. Torn and complete-but-undelimited final records must return journal_no_progress promptly, retain the exact source and pending events, then succeed after the real delimiter is appended. Empty batches with real offset progress remain accepted. Guard added after successful non-EOF ingest; native post-fix qualification pending. Native post-fix run41924556519 at9a8ebad passes the selected regression cases individually and reversed, with full production compile and90/90 native hotstring E2E. HTTP E2E was not selected.

findings.title: Legacy terminator migration reuses occupied record and state keys
findings.reproduction: Native run41924556519 at9a8ebad: both existing-record and future-false-state cases acknowledge migration but the actual engine omits the legacy character; fresh allocation and existing-character controls pass, individually and reversed.
findings.root_cause: HotstringsTerminatorMoveLegacy assigns custom_<codepoint> without reserving the admitted raw record and state namespace. An existing record or future false state can shadow a newly migrated character. The ordinary UI already owns a collision-free allocator.
findings.silent_failure: An acknowledged delimiter migration silently changes matching behavior and may disable a newly imported terminator.
findings.regression_test: Four terminator-move key allocation cases exercise real source admission, ConfigCommitUpdates and runtime projection, including second-boot idempotence. The fix reserves the raw namespace and uses _HotstringsTerminatorFreshKey; native post-fix execution pending.

findings.title: Terminator string membership merges case-distinct Unicode characters
findings.reproduction: Native run41924556519 reproduces seven lowercase engine/preview failures with uppercase controls passing, plus both exact-consumption migration failures with both/neither controls passing. Four Unicode-boundary/magic-membership probes stop on a missing headless validation helper and do not qualify those paths.
findings.root_cause: Windows terminator consumers use the default case-insensitive InStr and StrReplace despite exact scalar record identity. This affects matcher, consumption, framing, boundaries, preview and legacy migration. Lua sibling membership is exact.
findings.silent_failure: Typing an unconfigured case-distinct character can trigger an expansion, consume user text, invent a boundary, alter retained framing or reset preview incorrectly.
findings.regression_test: Twenty-two probes cover genuine engine and public migration consumers. All identified character-set comparisons now request case sensitivity. Four fixture prerequisite repairs and complete post-fix native qualification pending; no per-call-site count.

findings.title: A deleted default personal section hides the entries of the displayed section
findings.reproduction: Native run41924556519 case29 reports pointer=deleted_section, dropdown=Alpha, source_entries=2, visible_entries=0. The live-default control passes; reverse replay agrees.
findings.root_cause: OpenPersonalEditor trusts a saved nonempty default_section even when no section has that identity. The native dropdown displays its first live item while the model and list still address the absent section.
findings.silent_failure: An apparently selected personal section can look empty and invite unnecessary recreation of existing entries.
findings.regression_test: Two personal-native-default-owner cases use the actual constructor and DDL control, require unchanged opening files/preferences, and compare the live list with real source entries. The fix chooses an existing section before projecting both controls; post-fix pending.

findings.title: An old personal section switch destroys a successor opened during native retirement
findings.reproduction: Native run41924556519 case32 observes destroys=1, newer_seen=1, newer_alive_after=0, final_section=beta, newer_is_current=0. The ordinary switch control passes; reverse replay agrees.
findings.root_cause: _SwitchEditorSection destroys its retired window and then unconditionally calls OpenPersonalEditor. Native WM_DESTROY callbacks can legitimately publish a newer session before that old call resumes.
findings.silent_failure: The older user operation closes and replaces a newer personal editor session.
findings.regression_test: Two personal-native-switch-owner cases reenter the public constructor from exact owned-window WM_DESTROY. The fix checks the retired session epoch and successor slot after Destroy, and removes the redundant stale model read. Post-fix pending.

findings.title: A stale personal editor constructor publishes a dead priority control
findings.reproduction: Native run41924556519 case34 proves parent_create=1, newer_seen=1, native_priority_alive=1, global_priority_matches=0 and priority_error=Error. The no-reentry control passes; reverse replay agrees.
findings.root_cause: OpenPersonalEditor assigns _PersonalEditorPrioCtrl during construction before its final session-epoch check. A successor created through native control notifications owns a live priority edit, but the older constructor overwrites the global and then destroys that obsolete control.
findings.silent_failure: The current visible editor retains a dangling priority-control reference and cannot reliably save its entry.
findings.regression_test: Two personal-native-constructor-owner cases observe real WM_PARENTNOTIFY creation, exact HWND ownership and a subsequent genuine save. The priority control remains private until atomically published with the admitted GUI/source at the final epoch check. Post-fix pending.

findings.title: A rebuild guard admission failure waits forever for a nonexistent peer
findings.reproduction: Native run41925176895 at81d5aae: a real directory at rebuild.lock requires the one-second rescue timer to remove the obstruction before acquisition returns; the real peer-handle release control passes, individually and reversed.
findings.root_cause: FSOpenExclusiveGuard returns the same zero for genuine sharing contention and all other native opening or file-type failures. _KLR_RebuildAcquire interprets every zero as peer ownership and loops without a build deadline.
findings.silent_failure: A wrong-type or inaccessible lock path leaves the statistics rebuild waiting indefinitely rather than reporting an admission failure.
findings.regression_test: Two klr-rebuild-guard-admission cases retain actual CreateFile/CloseHandle behavior and bounded rescue, plus an added caller case verifying the prior published SQLite image and exact ledger remain intact. The adapter now reports Contended only for sharing/lock violations; other failures return promptly. Post-fix pending.

findings.title: Capacity eviction invokes the failure callback of an already cancelled request
findings.reproduction: Native run41925176895 at81d5aae: actual RawPost, CancelAsync and successor admission at capacity1 yield predecessor_callbacks=1 instead of0. Both real facade handles retire, both controlled native jobs spawn, and the successor completes. The live-eviction control delivers its one trimmed failure as expected; reverse agrees.
findings.root_cause: _LLMRemote_TrimAsyncRegistry detaches and cleans up the oldest request but calls its on_fail callback without honoring the cancelled flag. CancelAsync deliberately marks logical cancellation before deferred cleanup.
findings.silent_failure: An explicitly cancelled request can later publish a stale error through a callback whose owner already revoked delivery.
findings.regression_test: Two remote-trim-cancel cases use the public request/cancellation pipeline and actual managed facade with controlled Job I/O. The fix suppresses only the cancelled predecessor callback while retaining cleanup and live eviction notification; post-fix pending.

findings.title: Remote usage casts and inferred totals overflow the signed native integer domain
findings.reproduction: Native run41924556519 at9a8ebad: the real classifier and managed Poll both accept a finite1e30 usage count as MININT, publish a negative inferred total and negative estimated cost. Individually valid MAXINT prompt plus1 completion also wraps the inferred total to MININT. Both normal controls pass, and actual callbacks and exact handle/registry retirement still complete in all modes.
findings.root_cause: _LLMRemoteExtractUsageRoot treats every nonnegative finite Number as safely castable to signed64 Integer and adds two valid counters without a representation check. JSON validity alone does not establish the native consumer domain.
findings.silent_failure: A successful response can publish negative usage totals and estimated costs even though its provider supplied nonnegative values.
findings.regression_test: Six genuine classifier/managed-completion probes plus an eight-row boundary test preserve valid response text, exact callback count and retirement. The fix admits only representable counts and infers a total only when subtraction proves the addition safe; otherwise total remains unknown0. No product token cap is introduced. Native post-fix pending.

findings.title: Sticky replay drops modifier flags released before the captured key is replayed
findings.reproduction: Native run41924556519 at9a8ebad: sticky-native-modifier-flags plain passes, shift fails after native capture reports EndMods=<+, Shift is released, and replay reaches the receiving F6 handler with Ctrl1/Shift0. Actual synthetic transaction is Critical, finalization is not Critical, and both canonical buffers remain unchanged. Same inverse result; input injection is confined to a verified owned Edit, not a claim about physical keys.
findings.root_cause: StickyModifier sends Hook.EndKey with only the selected sticky modifiers and discards Hook.EndMods. A native captured modifier may already be released when Wait unwinds, so current key state or Blind cannot restore the captured shortcut.
findings.silent_failure: For example sticky Ctrl followed by Shift+F6 becomes Ctrl+F6, changing the requested application action.
findings.regression_test: The two real-hook/native-receiver probes include the production HS_RunSyntheticInputTransaction and TextPressKey pipeline. The fix unions captured Ctrl/Alt/Shift/Win groups with the sticky modifier without duplicates; it does not claim preservation of left/right modifier identity. Post-fix qualification pending.
